segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Behind the Hargrove mill the drying racks stood out in the open yard, under a slant roof with no walls, so the wind could get at the leaves. Garret Marsh lifted one off its cord with two fingers and held it up to the light for Elin to see the vein running down the middle of it.

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: Tell me what you've got there.

segments.speaker: Elin Hargrove
segments.text: Silver. Stem to tip, no break in it.

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: Then whoever cut it cut it right.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He laid it in the counting tray. The rule was older than the trade it fed, and it ran to a single sentence. A glass leaf is cut when the centre vein has gone silver the whole way, and never a day sooner. Cut green, it still looks like a leaf. It still hangs on a cord at a traveller's saddle. It simply never sounds.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Elin reached for the next one along, where the silver stopped two thirds down and went grey. Garret caught her wrist.

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: Not that one.

segments.speaker: Elin Hargrove
segments.text: It's nearly there. Another week hanging and nobody could tell.

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: Nearly is no good to a man standing in a hollow of bad air. Twenty-two years I've cut in this wood, and the rule has not failed me once. An early leaf lies to you quietly. You find out the one time you needed it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He let go and went back to sorting. Elin rubbed her wrist and said nothing, which she thought a considerable act of discipline.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A mule came up the lane at a walk and stopped at the gate. The woman leading it did not tie it off. She crossed the yard with her hat still knotted under her chin and a bundle of leaves in her fist.

segments.speaker: Dessa Fenwick
segments.text: Which of you knows these?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She put them down on the sorting bench. Six leaves strung on a cord, travel-stained, with a wooden tag at the knot.

segments.speaker: Dessa Fenwick
segments.text: Dessa Fenwick. I run Ashfall to Tollgate. Day before yesterday my mule stopped at the lip of a hollow and would not go down. I kicked her on, because these were hanging off my saddle and these were quiet. Three steps in and the ground tipped under me. She hauled me back up the slope by my own reins.

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: And they never sounded.

segments.speaker: Dessa Fenwick
segments.text: Not a whisper. I'd like to be told it was my own carelessness. I'd honestly rather hear that.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Garret shook the bundle beside his ear. Nothing came off it at all. He turned the tag over to the mark burned into the back of it.

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: Odell's mark. Batch eleven, this autumn's cut.

segments.speaker: Elin Hargrove
segments.text: Who cut eleven?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Garret read the number twice and set the tag down carefully, as though it might go off.

segments.speaker: Garret Marsh
segments.text: Every harvester this side of the wood cuts under Mabel Odell or under me, and I know each one of them by their shears. Nobody I know cut these.
